answer: Promotion out of probation needs 9 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. Because the island record is per identity, the kernel audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, as each alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's sonnet standing. A farm of 192 pays that 86 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
